structure: repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend on main at 59fa027: the Import Notification Service front door, a Hapi and Nunjucks app. Its pages live in src/server/app (about 30,000 lines with unit tests, about 9,000 without). src/server/app/features holds the routed features, listed in features/index.js: dashboard (the INS home at '/', about 260 lines of code and template plus a 137-line fit spec), notification-type (the choose-a-notification-type page and the hand-over into the animals and plants journeys, about 270 lines plus a 179-line fit spec), and address-book (about 4,000 lines of code, templates and copy plus about 4,000 lines of fit specs and fit helpers in address-book/fit): the list with tabs and type filter, add with its address-type step, view, edit and delete for addresses, and transporter type, private and commercial add, view, edit and delete pages, plus the hand-off context, journey registry and return-to logic that let a journey borrow the address book. address-lookup-spike is a dev-and-local-only page routed from app/routes.js. src/server/app/shared holds the layout, error templates, page kit, paths, list-page helper and shared copy (English and Welsh); page-maturity holds the maturity banner; app/auth holds the sign-in templates; lib/validate the form validators; services the address-book, transporters, ins-backend, countries and address-lookup clients and their stubs; docs the repo's own feature and architecture notes. There is no rulings or decisions ledger in the repo (no spec/ or decisions file). Left out of scope: the server plumbing in src/auth, src/plugins, src/config and src/server outside app (sign-in mechanics, CSRF, session cache, logging, health), the client JavaScript and stylesheets, the lighthouse tooling, the unit tests (*.test.js; the fit specs are the scope's tests), src/server/common/test-helpers except the journey hand-shake helper, and the developer process docs docs/testing.md, docs/lighthouse.md and docs/add-a-page.md. The capture fixture services/_capture/fixtures/countries.json is reference data, MDM's content, and is not read. The scope is cut into 8 parts by what a user sees.

parts.title: Shared layout, copy and page kit
parts.scope: Everything shared by every page: the layout, header, footer, service navigation, phase and maturity banners, error pages, error summary, page title rule, the page kit and paths, the list-page helper, the shared copy in English and Welsh, the sign-in templates, and the repo's own notes on how a page and a feature are built. Stops at any one feature's own pages.
covers: The layout: service name, header and service navigation links, footer, phase banner, skip link, language and every shared copy string in copy.en.js, with its Welsh twin in copy.cy.js
The page maturity banner: each maturity level in levels.js, its copy in English and Welsh and which pages show it
The error page and error summary templates: every heading and message
The page title rule the page-title fit spec asserts, and every page title it lists
Every route path in shared/paths.js and the list-page paging helper's page size and behaviour
The 4 sign-in templates: every heading, paragraph, button and link
Every test in page-title.fit.spec.js and smoke.fit.spec.js, and the error-focus and axe checks the fit suite holds pages to
The conventions docs/architecture.md, features.md and services.md record for pages, copy, validation, client JavaScript and service calls, as existing rulings

parts.title: INS home dashboard
parts.scope: The INS home at '/': its heading, the controls and links it offers, the notification list it shows from the INS backend read model, and the ins-backend client and stub that feed it. Stops at the notification type page the home links to.
covers: The dashboard page: route, heading, caption, every control, link and button, the empty state, every table column and how each cell reads, status tags, sort, filters, search and paging if any, and every error or outage message
Every copy string in dashboard copy.en.js and its Welsh twin
What the ins-backend client requests and what the stub returns, as the fields the list shows
Every test in dashboard.fit.spec.js

parts.title: Notification type and journey hand-shake
parts.scope: The choose-a-notification-type page and where each choice sends the trader (the animals and plants journey set bases), and the hand-shake by which a journey in another frontend borrows the address book and is returned to: the handshake context, the journey registry, return-to and the success message. Stops at the address book pages themselves.
covers: The notification type page: route, heading, every radio option with label and hint, the validation error message verbatim, the button, and where each option leads
Every destination in destinations.js and every journey set base in journey-set-bases.js

The hand-shake: which journeys are registered, what a journey passes in, which returns are honoured and which refused, what the trader sees while borrowing the address book, and the success message on return
Every copy string in notification-type copy.en.js and its Welsh twin
Every test in notification-type.fit.spec.js

parts.title: Address book list
parts.scope: The address book list page: its tabs, type filter, search, sort, paging, rows and actions, and the address-book service client, stub and address types that feed it. The shared address-book copy file is read in full, but only the list's keys are claimed here. Stops at the add, view, edit and delete pages and the transporter tab's own pages.
covers: The list page: route, heading, caption, each tab and what it lists, the type filter options, search box and its label and hint, sort, page size and pagination, every table column and how each cell reads, the empty states, the add buttons and row links, and every error message
The address types and roles in address-types.js and how they group, and what the client sends and receives when listing (roles, search, page, page size)
The list's keys in address-book copy.en.js and their Welsh twins
Every test in list.fit.spec.js

parts.title: Add an address

The shared address-book copy file is read in full, but only the add and address-type keys and the shared field keys are claimed here. Stops at view, edit and delete.
covers: The address-type page: route, heading, every option with label and hint, the error message verbatim, the button and where each option leads

The add page: route, heading, caption, every address field with its label, hint, width, autocomplete and whether it is required, the country select and how its list reads, every validation rule with its error message verbatim, the buttons and links, and what is saved

parts.title: View, edit and delete an address
parts.scope: One saved address: its view page, edit page and delete confirmation, and what each saves or removes. The shared address-book copy file and address-fields template are read in full, but only the view, edit and delete keys are claimed here; the field rules themselves belong to part 5.
covers: The view page: route, heading, every summary row and how it reads, the change, edit and delete links, and the back link
The edit page: route, heading, every field and how it is prefilled, the validation messages it shows, the buttons and what is saved
The delete page: route, heading, the warning and summary, the confirm and cancel actions, the success message and where it returns
The view, edit and delete keys in address-book copy.en.js and their Welsh twins
Every test in view.fit.spec.js, edit.fit.spec.js and delete.fit.spec.js

parts.title: Transporters
parts.scope: Transporter management in the address book: the transporter type question, the private and commercial add pages, the transporter view, edit and delete pages, their fields, navigation and saving, and the transporters service client and stub. The shared address-book copy file is read in full, but only the transporter keys are claimed here. Stops at the list's transporter tab, which belongs to part 4.
